en.headline: Privacy commissioner supports tighter land records access rules
en.dek: Ada Chung said misuse of land registry data for doxxing is worsening and journalists have no blanket exemption under the proposed arrangements.
body: Privacy Commissioner Ada Chung expressed support on Friday for the government’s proposed tighter rules on accessing land records, saying the changes would clarify purposes and better protect owners’ privacy.

Chung said her office had received 20 complaints over five years about alleged misuse of land registry data, including for cyberbullying and doxxing of owners, with six such cases this year alone, indicating a worsening trend.

She noted that under the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, there is an exemption for journalistic activities only when publication is in the public interest, and the new arrangements similarly require a public-interest purpose for certain searches. The government has tabled subsidiary legislation for the changes in the Legislative Council.

zh.headline: 私隱專員支持收緊土地查冊安排
zh.dek: 鍾麗玲表示土地登記冊資料被用於起底的情況有惡化跡象，傳媒亦無全面豁免。
body: 個人資料私隱專員鍾麗玲周五表示支持政府收緊土地查冊的建議安排，認為新規定可釐清目的，並更好保障業主私隱。
鍾麗玲說，公署過去五年接獲20宗涉嫌濫用土地登記冊資料的投訴，包括用於網絡欺凌及起底，今年已有六宗，趨勢惡化。
她指出，根據《個人資料（私隱）條例》，新聞活動使用個人資料有豁免，但前提是符合公眾利益；新安排中以公眾利益為目的的查冊亦須符合相關要求。政府已向立法會提交相關附屬法例。
